currency_exposure.fx_convention: USD/THB = baht per dollar. A RISE is a WEAKER baht.
currency_exposure.scope: ex-gold (gold sleeve unit count not tracked in this snapshot series)
currency_exposure.headline: By listing currency the book is 100.0% THB. By the currency the underlying businesses actually earn, roughly 34.9% of it is USD-linked. The concentration screen sees the first number and none of the second.
currency_exposure.net_position_read: Portfolio beta to a 1% baht depreciation is estimated at +0.09%. The book is therefore NET LONG the US dollar / NET SHORT the baht in economic terms, which is the opposite of what a '100% Thailand' label implies. A weaker baht is, on these assumptions, mildly HELPFUL to this specific portfolio.
currency_exposure.what_this_does_not_change: This does not reduce COUNTRY risk. A Thai political, regulatory, SET-liquidity or sovereign event hits all four positions regardless of what currency the revenue is denominated in. Look-through FX exposure and country concentration are different risks and this module only addresses the first. The 100% TH country flag from rebalancer.single_name_concentration_review() STANDS.

currency_exposure.magnitude_caveat: The spread across this table is small relative to a single day's equity move. That is the honest finding: for a book this size, FX is a real but second-order driver of value, and it is a FIRST-order driver only of the gold sleeve. Sizing decisions should not be made on this table alone.
currency_exposure.betas_are_assumptions_not_measurements: To replace these structural assumptions with measured betas, load a 3-year daily series of BAFS.BK / PTTEP.BK / SCB.BK closes and USDTHB into data/research/, then regress each name's daily THB return on the USDTHB daily return with Brent as a control. Until that exists, every beta in this module is an assumption with a stated rationale, and the report says so on every line.
